summary.intent: Execute GSD phase 68.1 for CipherBox (wiring the v2.0 web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain) through wave-based execution, multiple gap-closure rounds, full verification, and the /ship-phase pipeline (verify/secure/validate/simplify/E2E/CodeRabbit/PR), then support live smoke-testing of the shipped branch.
summary.outcome: All 33 plans executed across four rounds; phase 68.1 verified PASSED 5/5 with two human-approved deferrals; PR #588 shipped with all CI green and MERGEABLE; post-ship smoke testing surfaced and fixed a real CAS-merge write-plane clobber bug plus a file size/modified-date display gap (shipped as a SealedChildRef mirror feature), and found one more shared-folder staleness bug (documented as a todo, not fixed).

repo: Local dev stack: API on :3000, delegated-routing mock on :3001 (mock-ipns-routing, in-memory store wiped on any restart — do not restart casually), web vite on :5173; docker postgres/kubo/redis/someguy/tee-worker.
mock-ipns-routing healthcheck used busybox `wget localhost` which resolves to ::1 while the app binds IPv4-only — fix is `127.0.0.1` in docker-compose.yml healthcheck.

Email OTP is only logged to console (`DEV OTP for <email>: <code>`) when `NODE_ENV === 'development' || !process.env.NODE_ENV`; an API started from the E2E .env sets NODE_ENV to something else, silently swallowing the code (argon2-hashed in Redis, unrecoverable) even though the request returns 200.

vite pre-bundles/caches the workspace-symlinked @cipherbox/sdk dist; rebuilding sdk/sdk-core dists requires restarting vite with --force to pick up changes — UI edits HMR in but new SDK logic (e.g. new uploads) does not take effect until restart.

CI's unit-test job only runs coverage for api/crypto/core/sdk-core/sdk/api-client — apps/web unit tests are NOT run in CI (web is covered by Playwright web-e2e only), so broken web unit test mocks can silently rot on main.
CodeRabbit CLI has a 150-file diff cap; large phase PRs must be split into directory-scoped review passes (apps/packages/tests) and CodeRabbit will also skip PR-level review above that cap.

SealedChildRef (read plane) is deliberately frozen to {name, ipnsName, generation, versionFloor, readKeySealed} with no size/mtime — file list size and modified-date were phase-63 stubs (`FileListItem.tsx` hardcoded '-' and formatDate(0)). Adding size/modifiedAt as optional, conditionally-serialized mirror fields on SealedChildRef keeps golden-vector back-compat (NODE-03 test) while giving zero-knowledge display data.

Owner-side shared-out folders are seeded isLoaded:true with children:[] and never re-resolve IPNS on cached navigation; the 30s root poll doesn't descend into unchanged-ipnsName subfolders — so a grantee's write into a shared folder isn't visible to the owner until the owner writes something themselves or reloads.
1Password SSH commit signing produces false-negative timeouts (exit 143) even when the commit lands — always verify with `git log -1` before retrying, never blind-retry.
`git stash` must never be used in this repo (shared refs/stash across worktrees) — two separate executor agents violated this mid-session and had to self-recover without `git stash pop`.

code.finding: moveItem originally left the moved child's WriteChildRef in the source write-body — files became permanently un-editable after being moved into a subfolder. Fixed by unsealing under source writeKey, keyed by node UUID (not the ipnsName-based childId param), and resealing under dest writeKey.

getWriteBodyParams fail-opens to {} on zero writeKey (D-03); a transient IPNS resolve miss on an already write-capable folder can seal an empty write-body, dropping the entire write chain — flagged as latent risk, deferred as a todo.

publishWithCas's 409-conflict path merged only the read-body (SealedChildRef[]) via mergeChildren, but the write-body was resealed with the stale closure writeChildren — silently dropping a concurrent writer's WriteChildRef. This is the exact write-plane clobber class phase 68.1 exists to prevent, reachable from ~10 owned+bin call sites. Fixed by unsealing the remote write-body and unioning writeChildren by childId.

navigateUp only re-derives the shared writeKey when isRootDepth is true; navigating to an intermediate subfolder of a nested write share restores it with a zero writeKey, so writes from that level fail until re-entering from the share root. Deferred as a documented known non-blocker.

sizeDisplay and dateDisplay were hardcoded phase-63 stubs ('-' and formatDate(0)) because SealedChildRef carried no size/mtime; fixed by mirroring plaintext size and modifiedAt into the sealed read-plane ref at all fresh-construction sites (upload, batch upload, createFolder, shared-write new file/folder).

Dev-mode OTP console logging is gated on NODE_ENV being 'development' or unset; an API instance started under the E2E .env (non-development NODE_ENV) silently drops the plaintext OTP even on a successful 200 send.

updateGrant test asserted 4 args but the controller forwards 6 (including writeDescriptorRef, clearWriteDescriptor added for write-grant support this phase) — stale test, not a regression in production code.

workflow: Background agents that launch long-running bash processes (e.g. full e2e suites) frequently lose their wake signal when the process completes and the transcript gets evicted — mitigate with an independent disk-based watchdog plus a SendMessage resume while the transcript is still warm, or a fresh continuation agent with explicit completed_state if evicted.

Session/quota limits can kill an agent mid-task leaving partial, uncommitted disk state — recovery requires inspecting the working tree, validating/completing the partial work inline, then committing, rather than re-running from scratch.
When multiple background fix agents run concurrently, keep them on strictly non-overlapping file sets so their edits can be trusted and committed independently without merge risk.

Full local Playwright suites abort per-file on first failure (describe.serial) — a low failed-test count can badly understate real breakage, since dozens of downstream tests in the same file never execute; isolating individual spec files is necessary to get true pass/fail signal.

Adversarial/independent verifier agents that re-run tests and re-read code themselves (not just trusting SUMMARY claims) caught issues (e.g. an un-approved gap, a real CAS-merge bug) that summary-trusting review would have missed.

friction: Multiple background executor/verifier agents lost their 'wake' after a long background suite run completed, requiring manual SendMessage nudges or fresh continuation agents.
Session/quota limits killed agents mid-task at least four separate times (planner, executor, ship-phase fix agents), each requiring inline recovery of partially-written disk state.
CodeRabbit CLI's 150-file cap forced directory-scoped review passes and caused the PR-level CodeRabbit review to be skipped entirely (207+ files).
1Password commit signing repeatedly reported false-negative timeouts, requiring `git log -1` verification before any retry to avoid double-committing.
Two separate executor agents violated the no-git-stash rule mid-task, requiring manual verification that no user stash entries were disturbed.
Playwright test-results/ and .last-run.json artifacts are wiped on every run and gitignored as .log — required renaming to .txt to persist evidence and harvesting screenshots before re-runs.
wrong `cd docker` leaking into later commands caused a false 'ROADMAP.md missing' scare.
vite required manual --force restarts multiple times to pick up rebuilt sdk/sdk-core dists, since stale pre-bundled deps silently served old logic even though the app appeared healthy.
.env files could not be read directly (permission denied) — required using env-var overrides instead when diagnosing secret/config mismatches.
OTP extraction blocked for a while because the request succeeded (200) but the code was never logged, requiring several rounds of API restarts and log tracing to find the root cause.
